summary:
## [1.7.0] - 2026-11-23

Release 1.7.0. Plugins and polish. Two new plugins connect the venue to the world around it: **Webhooks** (another
system runs a preset here; this server tells another system what happened) and **Game triggers** (a preset when a
chosen team's game starts or ends). Lights now play effects themselves where the brand can, and Roku and Fire TV /
Android TV players are plugins like Apple TV. Underneath, every plugin is described by a manifest, is handed only
the parts of the server it declares, and is supervised on its own, so one that fails is restarted alone. On the
screen: every sheet and dialog is a proper modal, tab bars work from the keyboard, anything that deletes asks first,
messages can be dismissed, pages say when they could not load, and the light theme is readable. Docs: user guide
4.17 and 4.19, how-to 46 to 48, troubleshooting 10, and "Writing a plugin" in `docs/development.md`.

### Added

- **Game triggers plugin** (Settings › Plugins › Game triggers): run a preset when a chosen team's game starts or
  ends, from the programme guide the server already keeps. A trigger is a team as the listings write it (matched
  as whole words, with other names and an optional sport), a preset for the start with minutes before, and one for
  the end with minutes after. The page lists what a team's name would catch as it is typed, the games coming up
  and what the triggers did; a game on several channels counts once; what fired is kept across a restart so a
  game is never acted on twice, and the end of a game under way is kept even after the guide stops listing it.
  **Paused** holds everything, **Run start now** tries a trigger, and both are commands a button or a preset can
  use. Docs: user guide 4.17, how-to 48, troubleshooting 10.
- **Webhooks plugin** (Settings › Plugins › Webhooks): connect the venue to other systems, both ways.
  - **Incoming hooks**: an address another system calls to run a preset or a few steps here (a point of sale, a
    wall button, an automation service). The address carries the hook's own token and is shown once; what the
    caller sends never chooses what runs; it works for a caller with no staff PIN; a wrong token, a hook switched
    off and an unknown hook answer the same. Optional signed requests (HMAC, five-minute window, no replays), a
    per-hook cooldown and a per-address rate limit. Every run and (once a minute) every refusal is in the Audit.
  - **Outgoing hooks**: an address this server calls for every action, preset steps, a controller going offline,
    server alerts, scheduled tunes or software updates. JSON, signed by default, three tries with a growing wait,
    at most 100 events waiting per hook. Never sent to this server itself or to link-local, multicast or broadcast
    addresses; a redirect is not followed; the address is resolved once and the connection goes to that result.
  - **Deliveries** lists the last fifty attempts. A hook that gave up turns the plugin Degraded.

  Docs: user guide 4.17, how-to 46 and 47, troubleshooting 10.

- **Lights play effects themselves where the brand can.** Until now only DMX ran an effect itself; Hue, Govee and
  WLED were sent one change at a time (about one a second for Hue and Govee, ten for WLED), so a fast strobe was
  not one. Now:
  - **WLED** runs strobe, pulse, colour cycle, rainbow and chase as the controller's own effects, at its full
